rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods, Design and measurement <U+2014> HOBO-U30 soil-moisture probes installed in a flood-irrigation and a mulched-drip section (0-200 cm, May-Aug 2017) plus monthly groundwater depth data from seven monitoring wells 2014-2018. Q2: Results, Changes in groundwater depth and Conclusions <U+2014> flood irrigation shows a stronger and quicker groundwater-level response to rainfall infiltration than mulched drip; at ~8 m depth flood area still responds to heavy monthly rainfall (rise of 0.98 m) whereas drip area shows no response at 6 m; authors state drip generates basically no irrigation return water. Q3: two independent methods <U+2014> in-situ soil moisture profile monitoring (Fig. 4) and groundwater well depth dynamics (Fig. 5). Q4: Results, Changes in soil moisture content / Fig. 4 <U+2014> infiltration measured as soil-moisture increases at 50, 100, 160 and 200 cm after each rainfall under both systems (e.g., 72 mm storm: +7% at 50 cm in flood area vs lagged +8.3% in drip area; +1.4% at 2 m after 14 d vs +0.9% after 19 d). Q6: Changes in groundwater depth / Fig. 5 <U+2014> groundwater response compared across the irrigation areas of Horqin Left Wing Middle Banner using 4 wells in mulched-drip area and 3 in flood area, i.e. irrigation-district scale. Q7: Results and Conclusions <U+2014> recharge response occurs only when groundwater is shallow enough (no response at 6 m under drip, ~8 m under flood) and, at depth, only when monthly rainfall exceeds ~300 mm. Q8: Changes in groundwater depth <U+2014> authors state that due to limited research conditions only soil moisture to 2 m was monitored while groundwater depth exceeded 3 m, so the direct link to recharge could not be observed at the plot.
rows.notes: The 'drip' treatment is drip irrigation under plastic film mulch; the study itself attributes much of the reduced rainfall infiltration to the impermeable mulch rather than to drip per se, and the claimed mechanism (return flows) is asserted rather than measured (no return-flow measurement; difference is in rainfall-recharge response). Single site/region, one season of soil-moisture data, no replication or dispersion statistics. Q2 answered yes because mulched drip irrigation is a form of drip irrigation and the comparison is flood vs drip system, but the confounding with mulch should be noted.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a single-site observational comparison (one soil-moisture section per irrigation method, 2017) plus regional well records; no statistical analysis or uncertainty reporting.
